collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — TALL TALES AND SELF-INTEREST (TT-01 to TT-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Boasting, stretched stories, little vanities, wanting the credit, the best seat or the bigger half. Most of it is harmless and funny; kind people can be boastful too. Nobody is exposed for the sake of it, and nobody needs a lesson.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager applauds their own new roof just as a friend comes round the corner: keep clapping, or pretend to swat a fly.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has just finished re-thatching (subject.his/her) own roof all by (subject.him/her)self, and it looks very fine. Nobody is around to see it. So (subject) stands in front of the hut and gives (subject.him/her)self a round of applause, just as (friend) comes round the corner.

choices.label: Pretend You Were Swatting a Fly

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) doesn't stop. "It's a very good roof," (subject.he/she) explains. (friend) looks at the roof, considers it, and joins in. (child), a child, arrives and claps too. Soon there is a little crowd applauding a roof. (subject) bows. It's one of the best moments of (subject.his/her) life.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) claps once more, at nothing. "Fly," (subject.he/she) says. "Ah," says (friend). "Big fly." "Very big." (friend) looks up at the roof. "Lovely roof, by the way." (subject) glows quietly all evening.
